function: DRL (PPO, TD3, A3C) jointly sets BS beamforming, active STAR-RIS amplitudes and phases, SBD reflection, power, and time split to maximize throughput (max-min rate) (pp. 7-8).
system: Massive MIMO BS (N=8, 16, 32 antennas), active STAR-RIS (M=16-128 elements, energy splitting), I=3 SBDs (single antenna) and SUEs, NOMA, 28 GHz carrier (pp. 3-4, 10-11).
method: Model-free deep RL: PPO (on-policy actor-critic), TD3 and A3C agents trained online for 30000 episodes of 200 steps; reward is the rate plus constraint terms (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: BS channels Rayleigh, ASRIS channels Rician (factor 10), 28 GHz, path-loss exponent 3, averaged over 100 random channels; no standard model or measured data (pp. 6, 9-10).
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in the same simulated environment per setting; random user positions; averaged over 100 random channels; sweeps of power and element counts, no unseen scenario (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Random RIS phases (no optimization), passive STAR-RIS, five passive backscatter relays [39] (all simulated with A3C); PPO, TD3, A3C compared with each other (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Sum throughput (max-min user rate, bps/Hz) versus episodes, harvested energy, BS and ASRIS power, element counts; convergence episodes; ASRIS power consumption in mW (pp. 10-13).
complexity: none: Table II lists actor/critic layer sizes only (p. 10); convergence reported in episodes, with no parameter count, FLOPs, or runtime.
q1_support: p. 6: "all communication channels with ASRIS are considered to be Rician, and all communication channels with BS are considered to be Rayleigh". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channels are mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "All simulation results are generated by averaging over 100 random channels". Figs. 4-8 sweep power, harvested energy, and element counts; the paper never states that an agent trained in one setting is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 12: "the RIS parameters have not been optimized by the agent" (random RIS phases, Fig. 9); p. 10: "A3C algorithm leads to an increase in the total information exchange rate compared to the other two methods" (PPO, TD3).
q4_support: p. 11: "amplifies the computational complexity and implementation challenges as the number of elements grows" is qualitative; Table II (p. 10) gives layer sizes and episodes only. No parameter count, FLOPs, or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 7: "simulate it using a python program"; p. 10: "averaging over 100 random channels". Own simulated channels; no code or data link, public dataset, or availability statement appears in pp. 1-15.
notes: Includes: DRL learns BS beamforming and active STAR-RIS amplitudes and phases jointly with power and time split, so it passes above_phy; area 3. q3 is a judgment call for the reviewer: the paper presents PPO, TD3, and A3C all as its own approaches, but PPO and TD3 are standard DRL algorithms applied to the same problem, and the non-learned baseline is random RIS phases (Fig. 9). Table II was read as an image of p. 10.
